papers.title: Connected Self Forcing: Beyond Local Learning in Video Autoregression
papers.abstract: To stream long videos while maintaining visual quality and temporal consistency, Self Forcing mitigates exposure bias through self-rollout training on self-generated histories with key-value (KV) caching. To keep memory manageable, it detaches historical caches, preserving forward dependencies between chunks but severing the backward gradient paths. We introduce Connected Self Forcing, a training framework that reconnects gradient paths across autoregressive chunks, allowing feedback from later predictions to guide how earlier context is generated. These connections go beyond historical KV-writing: gradients pass through generated latents into the computations that produced them, linking the generation of earlier context to its use in later predictions. To make this connected training memory-efficient, we develop shortcut gradient replay, which recovers cross-chunk gradients without retaining the full rollout computation graph. Integrated with distribution matching distillation, Connected Self Forcing trains historical chunks according to both their direct supervision and their contribution to subsequent generation. Experiments on autoregressive video generation show improvements in long-horizon visual quality and temporal consistency, without changing the inference procedure.
papers.summary_cn: 论文指出，Self Forcing 虽然通过自生成历史训练缓解了训练与推理的不一致，但为节省内存而分离历史 KV 缓存，会切断后续视频块对早期块生成过程的反向监督。Connected Self Forcing 通过 Shortcut Gradient Replay 重建选定的跨块梯度，使历史块同时根据自身生成质量及其作为后续上下文的作用进行优化。该方法不增加模型参数、不改变推理流程，并在 60 秒和 240 秒自回归视频生成实验中改善了视觉质量、主体一致性和场景稳定性，减少了长时间生成中的漂移。
papers.contribution_cn:
1. 识别了 Self Forcing 中的前向依赖与反向学习信号之间的差距：生成块会影响后续预测，但历史缓存分离会阻断后续损失对早期上下文生成的梯度反馈。
2. 提出 Connected Self Forcing，通过 Shortcut Gradient Replay 经由历史 KV 状态恢复跨块梯度，而不保留完整自回归计算图。
3. 设计了面向内存效率的重放机制，以额外计算换取较低的激活内存，并避免递归重放整个早期生成轨迹。
4. 将跨块反馈与分布匹配蒸馏结合，使每个历史块同时接受直接 DMD 监督和来自后续生成的监督。
5. 在 60 秒和 240 秒长视频评测中展示了更好的视觉质量、主体与背景一致性及较少的长期漂移，且无需修改推理过程。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与研究重点高度相关，核心针对因果、自回归、流式和长视频生成中的训练问题。它使用自生成历史、KV 缓存和分块回滚训练，直接改善了长时间自回归生成的时间一致性与误差累积。Shortcut Gradient Replay 属于缓存复用和重计算换内存的训练机制，能够在不改变实时推理路径的情况下引入未来预测对历史生成的反馈。其结合分布匹配蒸馏和四步去噪，也与少步生成和生成加速相关。论文主要聚焦通用文本到视频生成，没有涉及动作条件控制、闭环交互世界模型或显式实时延迟评测。
papers.limitations_cn: 该方法需要通过重放部分生成和 KV 写入计算来恢复梯度，以计算换取激活内存，训练计算开销会增加。它只恢复选定的跨块路径，并在目标历史块处终止反馈，并非完整的全序列反向传播，因此不能涵盖所有长期梯度依赖。实验主要基于 Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B、DMD 后训练、四步采样和有限的提示词评测，外推到其他模型、任务和更复杂条件控制场景的效果仍需验证。方法的质量、动态程度和一致性表现依赖初始化方式；消融实验显示，降低跨块反馈权重可能损害部分质量和一致性指标。论文未明确说明实际流式部署中的端到端延迟、吞吐量和训练总计算成本。
papers.abstract_cn: 为了在保持视觉质量和时间一致性的同时流式生成长视频，Self Forcing 通过在模型自生成历史上进行自回滚训练，并结合键值（KV）缓存，缓解了暴露偏差。为控制内存开销，它将历史缓存从计算图中分离，在保留块之间前向依赖的同时切断反向梯度路径。我们提出 Connected Self Forcing，一种重新连接自回归块间梯度路径的训练框架，使后续预测的反馈能够指导更早上下文的生成。这些连接超越了历史 KV 写入：梯度会穿过生成的潜变量，进入产生这些潜变量的计算过程，从而将早期上下文的生成与其在后续预测中的使用联系起来。为使这种连接式训练具备内存效率，我们提出 Shortcut Gradient Replay，在无需保留完整回滚计算图的情况下恢复跨块梯度。结合分布匹配蒸馏，Connected Self Forcing 根据历史块的直接监督及其对后续生成的贡献共同训练这些块。在自回归视频生成实验中，该方法提升了长时间范围的视觉质量和时间一致性，同时无需改变推理过程。

papers.title: Conditional Residual Prediction: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion without a Bidirectional Teacher
papers.abstract: Causal video diffusion models generate video autoregressively, which suits streaming, interactive, and long-video generation. Under standard training, however, they often yield lower generation quality than bidirectional models of the same size. Many existing approaches address this gap by initializing from or distilling a pretrained bidirectional teacher. We instead train a causal model from an image-model initialization, with no bidirectional video model at any stage. Because this path requires neither a large bidirectional teacher nor a complex distillation pipeline, it is simpler and more scalable. On this path, we find that a causal model trained on ground-truth history becomes strongly dependent on it, so that at inference errors in its own generated history propagate forward. We hypothesize that much of this dependence is unnecessary, because the current input already determines much of what the history provides. We propose Conditional Residual Prediction (CRP), a simple recipe for reducing a model's reliance on a condition: the model first predicts the target without the condition, and the condition may only add a residual on top of this prediction. Applied to history, CRP makes the model predict each chunk from the present as far as it can and use the past only for what the present cannot supply. In controlled experiments, CRP nearly closes the 6.14-point gap to a bidirectional model trained under the same setup. Scaling this recipe, we train Optica, a 2B-parameter causal video model that autoregressively generates 5-second 480p videos and reaches 82.78 on VBench with only about 15M training videos.
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究因果视频扩散模型在自回归推理中的历史过度依赖问题。教师强制训练使用无误的真实历史，使模型学会依赖历史来建模当前输入本身已经能够确定的信息；推理时，模型自身生成历史中的误差因此会累积并传播。作者提出条件残差预测（CRP）：历史无关分支先根据当前噪声输入和文本条件进行完整预测，历史条件分支仅预测历史带来的残差，并通过停止梯度和隐空间融合避免分支相互污染。作者还以逐帧独立编码的图像VAE替代具有因果时间耦合的视频VAE，以减少潜变量间的历史依赖。在4M视频的受控实验中，CRP将因果模型与双向模型的VBench差距从6.14分缩小到0.19分，加入图像VAE后进一步达到略高于双向基线的水平。扩展训练得到2B参数的Optica，在约15M视频上训练后，以50步自回归生成5秒480p视频，在VBench上取得82.78分，且未使用双向视频模型进行初始化或蒸馏。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出条件残差预测（CRP），将条件信息限制为对无条件预测的残差，从而降低因果视频模型对历史信息的非必要依赖并缓解曝光偏差。该方法在同一网络中使用历史无关分支和历史条件残差分支，通过停止梯度与逐块隐空间融合实现，无需额外参数。 2. 从信息分解角度提出“历史过度依赖”假设，区分当前输入可提供的历史无关信息与只能由过去提供的历史专属信息，并用自回归质量下降和历史扰动实验验证该现象。 3. 以逐帧独立编码的图像VAE替代因果视频VAE，消除VAE引入的时间耦合和早期潜变量误差传播，同时通过轻量时间块层保持DiT计算成本基本不变。 4. 通过系统消融证明CRP的输出组合、停止梯度和隐空间融合均有独立作用；在受控设置下将因果模型与双向模型的VBench差距从6.14分缩小至0.19分，图像VAE进一步缩小至-0.20分。 5. 训练Optica这一2B参数、无需双向视频教师的因果视频模型，仅使用约15M训练视频，在5秒480p自回归生成任务上达到82.78的VBench Total分数，并展示其作为未来因果蒸馏教师和长上下文压缩基础的潜力。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接针对因果、自回归和流式视频生成，采用严格因果时序建模与KV缓存友好的自回归生成流程，能够生成5秒480p视频。CRP通过减少对已生成历史的非必要依赖，缓解自回归误差累积和长序列滚动中的曝光偏差；这一机制对长视频生成、交互式生成和闭环世界模型尤其有价值。论文还提供了不依赖双向教师的原生因果训练路径，可作为后续少步蒸馏、实时生成和因果世界模型的教师模型。其图像VAE设计降低了潜变量间的时间误差传播，但以牺牲时间压缩为代价；当前模型仍使用50步采样，因此与实时生成和高效部署的关系主要体现在方法潜力而非已验证的实时性能。论文未直接研究动作条件、闭环控制或视觉世界模型，但其历史建模、误差抑制和因果滚动机制可迁移到这些场景。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确说明的局限包括：所有受控实验和扩展实验仅评估5秒视频，尚未验证CRP能否在更长的自回归滚动中持续抑制误差累积；CRP目前只将历史作为条件，尚未研究图像到视频生成中的条件图像等其他可能被模型过度依赖的条件；当前Optica不支持图像到视频生成；图像VAE放弃了时间压缩，历史无关分支还增加了一次前向传播，因此当前50步模型未展示实时效率；作者尚未将Optica蒸馏为少步模型。此外，Optica的视觉质量仍低于部分双向或双向教师蒸馏模型，且实验主要基于内部视频数据和VBench短视频评测。
papers.abstract_cn: 因果视频扩散模型以自回归方式生成视频，适用于流式、交互式和长视频生成。然而，在标准训练下，其生成质量通常低于相同规模的双向模型。许多现有方法通过从预训练双向教师模型初始化或进行蒸馏来弥合这一差距。我们则从图像模型初始化开始训练因果模型，整个过程中不使用双向视频模型。由于该路径既不需要大型双向教师模型，也不需要复杂的蒸馏流程，因此更加简单且易于扩展。在这一训练路径中，我们发现，使用真实历史训练的因果模型会严重依赖历史信息，导致推理时自身生成历史中的误差向前传播。我们假设，这种依赖有很大一部分是不必要的，因为当前输入已经决定了历史所提供的大部分信息。为此，我们提出条件残差预测（Conditional Residual Prediction，CRP），这是一种降低模型对条件依赖的简单方法：模型首先在没有条件的情况下预测目标，条件只能在此预测之上添加残差。将其应用于历史信息后，CRP使模型尽可能仅根据当前信息预测每个片段，并只利用过去信息补充当前信息无法提供的部分。在受控实验中，CRP几乎弥合了相同设置下训练的因果模型与双向模型之间6.14分的差距。在此基础上，我们训练了Optica，一个拥有20亿参数的因果视频模型，能够以自回归方式生成5秒、480p视频，仅使用约1500万个训练视频便在VBench上达到82.78分。

papers.title: MORCA: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cache Reuse in Video Diffusion Acceleration
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve remarkable performance in video synthesis, but their iterative denoising process suffers from high inference latency. To address this, caching has emerged as an effective acceleration strategy by capitalizing on inter-step redundancy during denoising. Existing dynamic caching methods typically estimate the error that cache reuse would introduce at each denoising step (step error) to guide cache decisions, whereas our concern is how much quality loss cache reuse would cause in the final generated video (terminal error). We show that step error does not directly correspond to terminal error and that latent information helps capture their relationship, thereby informing cache decisions. Moreover, existing threshold-based methods cannot provide precise speedup control, making it difficult to meet practical requirements for user-specified acceleration targets. To address these limitations, we introduce MORCA, a cache scheduling framework trained through offline-to-online reinforcement learning to make latent-aware reuse/recompute decisions under user-specified acceleration targets. Extensive experiments on different video generation models across multiple target acceleration ratios demonstrate that MORCA achieves better generation fidelity than state-of-the-art caching methods under comparable computational budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/x10ngyx/MORCA.
papers.summary_cn: MORCA针对视频扩散模型迭代去噪延迟高的问题，研究缓存复用中的步骤误差与最终视频质量损失之间的不一致性。该方法将缓存调度建模为带复用预算约束的MDP，利用去噪步骤统计、潜变量特征和剩余复用预算，由潜变量感知调度器逐步决定重新计算或复用缓存，并采用基于IQL的离线到在线强化学习进行训练。实验在Wan2.1和Wan2.2上表明，MORCA能够较精确地满足目标加速比，并在多种加速设置下取得优于TeaCache、MagCache、DiCache和SeaCache的速度—质量折中。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出MORCA潜变量感知的自适应缓存调度框架，用于视频扩散推理加速。2. 发现步骤误差不能充分预测终端误差，并使用当前、前一步及最近一次重新计算时的潜变量压缩特征来改善终端误差相关的缓存决策。3. 将用户指定的目标加速比转换为复用步数预算，构造带预算约束且保证约束可满足的增强MDP，从而实现更精确的加速控制。4. 引入基于隐式Q学习的离线到在线强化学习范式，以有限的离线轨迹初始化调度器，再通过在线数据探索和微调提升性能。5. 在Wan2.1和Wan2.2上的实验显示，该方法在相近延迟和加速比下改善了PSNR、SSIM及LPIPS等指标。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作直接聚焦视频扩散生成的实时推理加速，属于研究重点中的缓存复用、推理加速和视频扩散方向。它针对DiT多步去噪中的跨步骤冗余，动态选择缓存复用或完整重计算，可降低视频生成延迟；同时结合潜变量状态、强化学习和显式复用预算，支持面向用户目标加速比的自适应调度。该方法不改变生成模型本身，因而可作为现有缓存粒度和复用策略之上的调度层，并有潜力与蒸馏、稀疏注意力等其他加速技术结合。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的实验主要覆盖Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B和Wan2.2-T2V-A14B两个模型，跨架构泛化能力论文未明确说明。训练需要代价较高的视频生成轨迹，且方法依赖预先校准复用步数与推理延迟或加速比之间的经验关系。复用步数是离散的，因此目标加速比无法完全精确实现，论文报告仍存在不可避免的控制误差。评估主要使用固定的VBench提示集合、PSNR、SSIM和LPIPS，并以相同提示和随机种子的无缓存结果作为参考；对真实用户体验、长视频时长扩展、不同硬件及更广泛模型的影响，论文未明确说明。作为调度级方法，其效果还依赖底层缓存粒度和复用策略；与其他缓存机制组合后的收益，论文仅将其作为未来方向。
papers.abstract_cn: 扩散Transformer（DiT）在视频合成中取得了出色的性能，但其迭代去噪过程带来了较高的推理延迟。为解决这一问题，缓存通过利用去噪过程中跨步骤的冗余，已成为一种有效的加速策略。现有动态缓存方法通常估计每个去噪步骤中复用缓存会引入的误差（步骤误差），并据此指导缓存决策；而我们关注的是复用缓存会对最终生成视频造成多大的质量损失（终端误差）。我们发现，步骤误差与终端误差并不直接对应，而潜变量信息有助于捕捉二者之间的关系，从而指导缓存决策。此外，现有基于阈值的方法无法精确控制加速比，难以满足用户指定的加速目标。为解决这些局限，我们提出MORCA，一种通过离线到在线强化学习训练的缓存调度框架，能够在用户指定的加速目标下，基于潜变量感知地决定复用缓存或重新计算。在不同视频生成模型和多个目标加速比上的大量实验表明，在相近计算预算下，MORCA相比现有先进缓存方法能够获得更高的生成保真度。代码已发布于https://github.com/x10ngyx/MORCA。

papers.title: LiteNWM: Efficient Latent World Models for Onboard Visual Navigation in the Wild
papers.abstract: Direct visual navigation policies generate trajectories efficiently but do not explicitly evaluate their future consequences. Generative navigation world models provide this foresight through visual rollouts, which are costly when evaluating multiple candidates. We present LiteNWM, a latent navigation world model that shares visual encoding across candidates and jointly predicts their action-conditioned future representations at multiple horizons, while a learned scorer uses these predictions to select trajectories. In offline evaluations on RECON, SCAND, and SACSoN, LiteNWM reduces macro-averaged trajectory error by 17.56% relative to NoMaD+NWM-XL and achieves a 128.00-fold end-to-end speedup on an RTX 5090. The same evaluator transfers from NoMaD to MBRA without proposer-specific retraining, reducing MBRA's macro-averaged trajectory error by 16.2%. In real-robot experiments in unseen indoor and outdoor environments, LiteNWM improves navigation success from 43.3% to 83.3% relative to NoMaD. These results demonstrate that LiteNWM can be deployed for future-aware planning and closed-loop navigation on a physical robot.
papers.summary_cn: Direct visual navigation policies generate trajectories efficiently but do not explicitly evaluate their future consequences.
papers.contribution_cn: We present LiteNWM, a latent navigation world model that shares visual encoding across candidates and jointly predicts their action-conditioned future representations at multiple horizons, while a learned scorer uses these predictions to select trajectories.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, efficient generation；关键词：world model, action-conditioned, closed-loop, efficient
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: UltraWorld: Learning Interactive Ultrasound World Models from Untracked Clinical Videos with Acoustic Sampling Map
papers.abstract: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations. Learning this action--observation relationship typically relies on synchronized video--pose pairs, which are costly to collect at scale and largely unavailable in routine clinical recordings. Reliable action following further requires modeling ultrasound's cross-sectional sampling geometry. We present UltraWorld, a self-distillation recipe that transfers priors from clinical ultrasound videos into interactive world models without real action annotations. Starting from clinical videos, we adapt a video foundation model into an ultrasound generator conditioned on reference images and anatomical masks. Anatomical masks sampled along programmable trajectories through 3D anatomy provide spatial guidance for synthesizing action--video pairs. We then use these synthetic pairs to self-distill the generator into a world model that predicts future observations from local observations and actions, without requiring anatomical masks or other 3D assets at inference time. To further improve action following, we introduce the Acoustic Sampling Map (AsMap), which represents probe poses and imaging settings as pixel-wise 3D sampling positions, beam directions, and depths. Experiments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity and action following. Across nine simulated closed-loop local planning episodes, UltraWorld reduces the mean final distance to the goal and orientation error by 29\% and 38\%, respectively, compared with visual servoing. Project Page: https://ultraworld-project.github.io/.
papers.summary_cn: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations.
papers.contribution_cn: We present UltraWorld, a self-distillation recipe that transfers priors from clinical ultrasound videos into interactive world models without real action annotations.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, efficient generation；关键词：world model, interactive, closed-loop, distillation
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: WAM-Cache: Staleness-Bounded KV Reuse for Efficient World Action Models
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) enable generalist robot manipulation by conditioning an action expert on representations from a pretrained video Diffusion Transformer (DiT). In closed-loop control, the video DiT runs at every chunk to encode the current observation into layerwise key-value (KV) pairs that the action expert queries. This prefill dominates the per-chunk computational cost, yet existing training-free accelerations leave it fully dense. We present WAM-Cache, a training-free framework that retains layerwise key-value representations across chunks and recomputes only a sparse refresh set of tokens. Crucially, we find that the intuitive heuristic of refreshing visually drifted tokens plateaus far below the dense baseline, even with an oracle predicting ground-truth KV drift. Downstream action accuracy is instead governed by where the action expert attends, not by what moved. WAM-Cache therefore selects the refresh set by uniting the action expert's cross-attention with visual latent surprise, complemented by a strict age bound that suppresses compounding error. On Fast-WAM, WAM-Cache cuts video DiT prefill FLOPs by 32-42% across RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and real-world experiments, while staying within 0.7-1.8 percentage points of the dense policy in simulation and 2.5 points on a real robot.

papers.title: Memory Forcing: Attendable Mid-Horizon History for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion enables causal video streaming without a bidirectional pass over the full clip, but existing few-step systems usually retain only the opening and most recent frames in a fixed-size KV cache. Once an event leaves this window, later frames can no longer attend to it, a failure we term mid-horizon forgetting. We present Memory Forcing, a few-step streaming method that preserves this missing history without increasing the cache size. Its Archive \& Working Banks partition the cache into sink, archive, and working regions, retaining diverse intermediate events alongside recent motion under fixed memory. Because absolute temporal indices drift outside the training range, Bank-aware RoPE reassigns indices at attention time so each bank remains distinguishable. At 1.3B, Memory Forcing leads on longer clips, shows the smallest drop from 5s to 60s among methods reporting all four lengths, and preserves subjects and scenes through leave-and-return. The same design scales to Wan2.2 5B, producing more physically plausible, realistic, and dynamic videos and, to our knowledge, the first public 5B model on this forcing line.

papers.title: Beyond Policy Support: Interaction Constrained Offline Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning enables reward-driven policy improvement from fixed datasets without requiring online exploration, making it particularly attractive in safety-critical domains. A central challenge, however, is distribution shift: policy optimization may favor actions that are weakly supported by the offline data, rendering value estimates unreliable. Existing approaches primarily control this shift in the policy's own action space. In interactive environments such as autonomous driving, this can be insufficient: a candidate ego trajectory may remain well supported under the marginal behavior distribution while being poorly supported jointly with the surrounding-agent behavior observed in the logged interaction. We refer to this degradation in interaction support as \emph{interaction distribution shift} (IDS), and introduce \emph{Interaction-Constrained Drive Policy} (ICDP), an offline reinforcement learning framework that explicitly controls interaction-level distribution shift. Starting from the joint data distribution over ego and surrounding-agent futures, we show that joint-support degradation decomposes exactly into an ego-support component and a residual interaction-support component. We recover the latter through contrastive density-ratio estimation, isolating interaction compatibility without explicit joint-density modeling, surrounding-agent prediction, or rollouts in reactive simulators or learned world models during policy optimization. Closed-loop evaluations on nuPlan, Interplan and real-world truck experiments show that ICDP suppresses high-value yet interaction-unsupported trajectory selections and improves performance in interaction-critical driving scenarios. Project webpage: https://mahmoud-selim.github.io/ICDP/

papers.title: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: World models in end-to-end autonomous driving predict future scene evolution to provide foresight for trajectory planning. Existing methods mainly study how to predict the future and how to use it, but less often ask which future representation is actually most useful for planning. To this end, we propose PlanWAM, a Planning-Shaped World Action Model. The key idea is to let the planning task shape the future-state representation, so that it retains the information most useful for planning. A latent world model then predicts this planning-shaped future latent representation from historical observations and uses it for planning, enabling foresighted planning. Specifically, we first use a Temporal Register Pyramid to compress multi-frame historical information in a recency-aware manner, learning a compact history representation oriented toward future reasoning and planning. We then introduce a privileged future posterior branch that observes ground-truth future frames, and shape its future latent representation with trajectory-planning objectives to obtain a planning-shaped future latent representation. Hindsight-to-Foresight Distillation trains a prior branch that depends only on history to predict this future latent representation. The predicted future latent representation serves as planning context and guides trajectory generation and selection. PlanWAM achieves 93.8 PDMS / 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v1/v2 navtest and reaches 38.7 HD-Score on closed-loop HUGSIM in a zero-shot setting, demonstrating leading planning performance across both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that planning-shaped future representations provide an effective and deployable form of foresight for world-action models.

papers.title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
papers.abstract: Video generators and video-based world models can synthesize plausible visual trajectories, but long-horizon procedural tasks require generation to adapt to what has actually been produced. A model must determine the next action from its generated state, execute that action, and recognize when the task is complete. Open-loop generation cannot adapt to execution outcomes, while existing closed-loop systems often rely on pretrained executors or indirect verification. This leaves a gap between deciding an action and successfully realizing it. We formulate procedural video generation as \emph{closed-loop task execution in visual world space} and introduce \textbf{WorldGuide}. Given only an initial image and a task goal, WorldGuide predicts an atomic action, generates its corresponding video clip, and uses the generated result to select the next action or terminate. The Planner and Executor are trained on the same step-level procedural demonstrations: the Planner learns to predict the next atomic action or task completion from visual progress, while the Executor is directly trained to realize the predicted actions. Hierarchical visual memory maintains state across long-horizon execution with bounded history token cost. Due to the lack of step-level action-video supervision for joint planner-executor training, we introduce \textbf{WorldGuide Bench}: approximately 59K step-annotated videos across 245 tasks and 27 procedural categories. WorldGuide achieves a 33.33\% Task Success on \textbf{WorldGuide-Bench}, compared with 29.90\% for the strong recent video model MiniMax-H3, even though MiniMax-H3 receives reference action plans, and achieves 47.69\% on \textbf{VideoCraft-Bench} compared with 32.73\% for MiniMax-H3 under goal-only conditioning. These results demonstrate the importance of coupling planning with learned execution for goal-directed procedural video generation.
